contract.unallocated.title: UNALLOCATED · Entry Agreement
contract.unallocated.warnings: Warnings: flashing lights, loud sounds, jump scares and psychological horror.
contract.unallocated.body: By continuing, you accept the data uses of this version. Everything stays on your computer. Your response lets us begin. Thank you for cooperating. Subject #4114.
contract.unallocated.input.hint: Press the button, or type it and press Enter.
contract.unallocated.input.retry: Type "I agree" to replace the selection.
contract.unallocated.uses.title: Data uses · What we receive
contract.unallocated.uses.current: In this build, during play: we read what you type in the world chat so the story can react (some lines are not shown); we use your player name inside the fiction; your position, where you look, whether you run and the blocks you break decide when events happen. On this screen we read whether a local acceptance exists and the text of the field (up to 64 characters), and we check your computer's clock when you accept.
contract.unallocated.uses.local: We store a single acceptance in unallocated/contract.properties, inside the game directory: UTC date and time, method (TYPED: text with Enter; CLICKED: button or Enter without text), the text you left in the field and the contract version. It is kept between games until you delete that file. It does not leave your computer. If we cannot save it, you can continue and it will appear again on restart. Minecraft's normal logs say that the mod loaded or whether there was an error; we do not copy your response into those logs. Story progress (chapter, events seen and attempts) is saved inside the world itself, like any other game.
contract.unallocated.uses.absent: This build does not capture microphone or camera, does not clone voices, does not write your Minecraft options and does not connect to AI services or the internet. We do not store what you type in chat; Minecraft may record it in its normal logs. Brief brightness changes and screen effects happen only in memory and end when you quit.
contract.unallocated.uses.future: There are no hidden uses and no advance collection: if a later version reads anything more, this list will change before it happens.
contract.unallocated.uses.lore: Subject #4114. Validation protocol — g0: estimate the human fear response. 1. Consent. 2. Blind subject. 3. Full curve: baseline → stimulus → peak → relief. 4. Erasure: raw data is deleted after processing. Success criterion (spec g0): success_threshold = 0.82. Your response is allocated.
story.unallocated.book.0: if you found this, you got in the same way i did. i left it in the base because it's the only door that still closes. read all of it before you go down the mine. and don't trust the tab list.
story.unallocated.book.1: there's someone standing on the hill to the north. every time you look at them through the spyglass they're closer. i stopped looking. you should too.
story.unallocated.book.2: the floor at the end of the mine gives way. down there it's this same server, only rotten. it killed me there. then it asked me if i agreed, and i was back up here.
story.unallocated.book.3: it looks like the chat gives you access to the server's internal console when you die. help, ls and cat answer. every death gets you deeper. the third time it let me stop processes. don't type too much. it listens.
story.unallocated.book.4: every error says UNALLOCATED. and reclaim, reclaim, reclaim. i looked the word up: on clusters, reclaim means taking back resources that belong to you.

intro.unallocated.title: UNALLOCATED
intro.unallocated.motd.1: Welcome back. We kept your spot.
intro.unallocated.explorer.0: Three days ago someone posted an address on a forum for dead servers. play.vallecraft.net. The thread has forty-one replies, and almost all of them say the same thing. It is still on.
intro.unallocated.explorer.1: ValleCraft was small. A few kids from the same town, four or five online on a good night, maybe a dozen names in all. In the summer of 2021 the admin stopped logging in. Nobody turned the server off. Nobody remembered it was still running.
intro.unallocated.explorer.2: Last week it showed up again on the server lists, running 26.3, with nobody online. Two people from the thread said they would go in that night and post screenshots.
intro.unallocated.explorer.3: There are no screenshots. Their last replies are from that night, and their accounts still show as online. You want to know what they saw.
intro.unallocated.former.0: In 2020 you played on ValleCraft almost every afternoon. Four or five of you on a good night. You had a house by the road and a helper rank you were proud of.
intro.unallocated.former.1: In the summer of 2021 the admin stopped logging in. No goodbye, no notice on the board. The rest of you waited a few weeks, and then, without anyone saying it, stopped going.
intro.unallocated.former.2: Nobody turned it off. Tonight it is back on your server list, running today's version, as if someone had been looking after it all this time.
intro.unallocated.former.3: Your account is still saved. The server says it kept your spot. Zuri and Noor show as online too, and neither of them has answered anyone in years.
intro.unallocated.invited.0: Kai was the one who got you into ValleCraft back in 2020. A small server, a few kids, the same faces every night. You had not thought about it in years.
intro.unallocated.invited.1: Kai has not been online for three days and has not answered a single message. Nobody you know has heard anything.
intro.unallocated.invited.2: Tonight, at last, a message from Kai's account. “come on, you have to see this. play.vallecraft.net”
intro.unallocated.invited.3: ValleCraft has been dead since 2021. Nobody ever turned it off. Kai answers nothing else, but the account shows as online, right now, on that server.

story.unallocated.puppetbook.0:
If you are reading this, it already caught you once. This is what I know.

When you die, choose "Not yet". You stay dead, as a Puppet, and you see its threads.
story.unallocated.puppetbook.1:
As a Puppet, and only then, the chat is its server's console. Type help. Then cat README and read my notes in home/noor.

If you type a lot, it hears you and comes down. Let it: every time it catches you, you get deeper.
story.unallocated.puppetbook.2:
The third time you can see its processes with ps. Find its own, the one eating everything, and stop it with kill and its number.

Once stopped, the contract tells you which number to give it. — Noor
